transfer_edges.rationale: Authentication-then-authorization stems are two sides of the same identity-control distinction.
Lifecycle Workflows are distinguished from access reviews, leaking the recertification proposition.
Defender for Cloud is defined as CSPM plus workload protection, which is the CSPM proposition.
Defender XDR suite composition names Defender for Endpoint as the endpoint workload service.
Privacy principles are taught as the companion topic to the Service Trust Portal.
Classification-before-DLP workflow items leak the DLP sensitive-sharing proposition.
Identity-as-perimeter and Zero Trust both reject implicit trust based on network location.
ID Protection risk signals are the identity-risk input Conditional Access is taught to evaluate.
Azure Firewall versus NSG discrimination restates the NSG allow/deny subnet-or-NIC proposition.
STP versus Compliance Manager discrimination restates Compliance Manager's customer-posture role.
Retention versus sensitivity-label discrimination restates sensitivity-label classification/protection.
Both identify Microsoft Sentinel as the cloud-native SIEM and SOAR service.
DDoS versus WAF discrimination restates DDoS Protection's volumetric network-layer role.
SOAR automation/playbook exposure materially transfers across the SIEM/SOAR and Sentinel mitigation leaves.
eDiscovery versus Audit discrimination restates Audit's searchable activity-record proposition.
NSG versus WAF discrimination restates WAF's HTTP application-layer role.
Vulnerability Management versus incident-response-console discrimination points at the Defender portal/XDR operations experience.
Audit versus Insider Risk Management discrimination restates the insider-risk internal-activity proposition.
Federation is taught as using a home identity provider to vouch for a user to a relying party.
Entra ID versus AD DS discrimination restates the directory-service identity-store proposition.
